HatchPattern__Grassland__Meta.Meta__Description: Grassland - fields, paddocks, lawns and open grass. Small five-blade tufts, a tall centre blade between four short ones, scattered sparsely in the Ordnance Survey manner. Drawn as an AREA texture: it says 'this is grass', it does not say where each tuft grows.
HatchPattern__Grassland__Meta.Meta__WhyTransparent: The tile paints TUFTS ONLY and never a background. The pale green wash under it is the fill deck of the site plan composite, a separate layer with its own colour and opacity, so either can be switched off on its own.
HatchPattern__Grassland__Meta.Meta__WhyOwnInk: The tufts carry their OWN ink, #43A047 - the woodland green - rather than 'inherit'. The Grassland tag draws its edges in the OS base map grey, so tracing a field over its OS boundary adds nothing to the linework, and an inherited ink would therefore paint grey grass. A hex here beats the layer's line colour, on screen and on paper.
HatchPattern__Grassland__Meta.Meta__WhyPaperUnits: Every length here is PAPER millimetres, like the dash patterns in Na__LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Config__.json, so a tuft measures the same on the sheet at 1:200 and at 1:500. Pattern__Scale on a viewport adjusts from there.
HatchPattern__Grassland__Meta.Meta__WhySparse: Ten tufts on a 28 x 26 mm tile, about one every 73 square millimetres - the density of the reference sheet. Grass covers whole fields, so it must be the quietest texture on the drawing: smaller and sparser than the woodland beside it.
HatchPattern__Grassland__Meta.Meta__WhyScatter: The positions are a blue-noise scatter, generated ONCE and written in below as fixed numbers, so screen and paper can never disagree. It was scored on a torus - the gap across a tile seam counts like any other gap - and against the three regularities that survive a repeat: two tufts sharing a column (an endless vertical line once the tile repeats), two sharing a row, and three nearly in line. No two tufts are closer than 6.8 mm. A skewed lattice was tried first and laid the tufts out in diagonal stripes across a field.
HatchPattern__Grassland__Meta.Meta__WhyInsideTheTile: Every tuft sits wholly inside the tile. A browser clips a <pattern> at its tile edge and the PDF stamper does not, so a tuft crossing the seam would print whole and show cut on screen.

HatchPattern__Grassland__Identity.Identity__Description: How this pattern is named, found and grouped in the Patterns panel.
HatchPattern__Grassland__Identity.Identity__Note: Referenced by 75__SitePlan__SoftLandscape__Grassland in the Tags SSOT, through SitePlan__FillHatchId.

HatchPattern__Grassland__Tile.Tile__Description: The repeating cell, in paper millimetres.
HatchPattern__Grassland__Tile.Tile__Note: The scatter already staggers, so no row offset is needed.

HatchPattern__Grassland__Defaults.Defaults__Description: What the pattern draws with before a viewport overrides anything. A stroke colour written as a hex is the pattern's own ink and beats the layer's line colour; 'inherit' would take the layer's.

HatchPattern__Grassland__Glyphs.Glyphs__Description: Drawn about the glyph's base centre, y pointing DOWN, in tile millimetres.

Tuft.Glyph__Note: Five blades on one baseline: a tall centre blade, a short one either side of it, and an outer pair leaning away. The lean of the outer pair is what makes it read as a tuft rather than a comb.

HatchPattern__Grassland__Placements.Place__Note: Upper band, left - 0.8 mm clear of the left edge
Lower band, right - 1.3 mm clear of the right edge
Bottom band, centre - its base 0.2 mm clear of the bottom edge

HatchPattern__Grassland__Bounds.Bounds__Description: How far a viewport may scale and turn this pattern before it stops reading as grass.
